summary: You produced a solid, well-motivated Great Barrier Reef monitoring mission with good SSO design, STK evidence, and clear launch and ground segment justification. You met most requirements strongly. To reach full marks, fix the RAAN definition, complete the link budget frequency, replace Wikipedia, and tighten report presentation.

criteria.C1: You did well defining your coral-reef monitoring concept on p.4-5, with bleaching rationale, fluid lensing, and clear users like CSIRO/BOM and single-satellite justification. This is Accomplished work. For top of band, add more quantitative literature on revisit needs.
criteria.C2: Strong main body: Vega E justification p.8, 600km SSO calculation p.11 with 97.79 deg inclination, and STK ground access p.13. To improve: p.12 RAAN 27.33 deg is not launch longitude - RAAN is inertial. p.11 missing communication frequency/link budget. Add maneuver details.
criteria.C3: Good summary on p.16 linking launch, SSO, ground station and EOL drag sail back to evidence. This is Accomplished. For higher, make conclusions more specific - e.g., quantitative coverage, revisit, and deorbit time - rather than generic configuration statement.
criteria.C4: Clear structure and labelled STK figures with executive summary p.2-3. To reach Accomplished: p.17 replace Wikipedia source [6] which brief forbids and fix bibliography formatting, and p.15 complete truncated EOL sentence 'to ‘ and is suitable' for professionalism.
